terms.gloss: capital letters, large letters (opposed to minūtae, small ones)
terms.comment: Plautus sets grandēs against minūtae, and Cicero speaks of a name cut in large letters; Traupman’s singular is littera grandis, with littera minūta for a small letter (245).

phrases.latin: Prīma littera nōminis tuī est T, majuscula.
phrases.english: The first letter of your name is a capital T.

sources: John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, supplied PDF (printed page numbers): pp. 28, 31.
